added_models.model: Hemophilia A dogs (Chapel Hill / Queen's colonies)

safety.judgement: Opening entry at the dog track's first use; the draft's dog track had no safety cell at all.
safety.note: Dog safety strip opens with the AAV2-cFVIII liver dogs; no human comparison yet.
safety.quote: These data support the use of AAV2 vectors in human clinical trials to treat hemophilia A patients.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 21081906, epub 2010-11-16); dogs received species-matched canine FVIII, the analogue of hFVIII in patients.
safety.judgement: Prediction recorded before any F8 gene-therapy member was dosed; still untested until a patient inhibitor result exists.
safety.note: The dog's stated on-target safety prediction: no lasting FVIII inhibitor after liver-directed AAV8/AAV9-cFVIII in 9 dogs over 24 dog-years.
safety.quote: Notably, no long-term immune response to FVIII was observed in any of the dogs (1/9 dogs had a transient inhibitor).

safety.magnitude_basis: FVIII inhibitor incidence after liver AAV-FVIII: dogs 0/9 long-term (1 transient) vs patients 0/9 at 52 weeks
safety.confidence_note: Paired by me: Rangarajan does not cite the dogs. n=9, one year; patients were inhibitor-history-negative, dogs were naive. Registry date is the NCT02576795 results posting.
safety.judgement: On-target harm (transgene immunogenicity) scored on the dog track; v3 rule 1 allows the drafter's pairing the draft called 'uncompared in print'. Kept in the gene-therapy modality strip because the dogs only ever modelled gene transfer.
safety.note: First nine valoctocogene recipients: no FVIII neutralizing antibodies through 52 weeks, as the dogs predicted (0/9 long-term).
safety.short: Patients: no FVIII inhibitors, as dogs
safety.quote: No neutralizing antibodies to factor VIII were detected.

safety.magnitude_basis: vector-attributed liver tumours: dogs 0/9 at up to 10 years (clonal expansions in 5/6 biopsied) vs patients 0 HCC and 2 non-attributed malignancies at ≤5.5 years
safety.confidence_note: SBRA text (2023-06-29) names NHP, not dog, integration data; patient follow-up (≤5.5 y) is shorter than the dog's 10 y and clonal expansion itself was not assessed in patients, so only the 'no tumours' half of Nguyen 2021 is tested. Also confirms 'No subjects developed an inhibitor to FVIII or thrombosis.' Registry date is the NCT03370913 results posting.
safety.judgement: Genotoxicity prediction (Nguyen 2021, epub 2020-11-16) folded into the strengthening entry rather than a separate status; a predicted clonal expansion is not yet askable of patients at this follow-up.
safety.note: Phase 3 package: 0/134 inhibitors and no HCC; two malignancies not vector-attributed by insertion-site analysis. Dogs: clonal expansions but no tumours at 10 years.
safety.short: No HCC or inhibitors at licensure
safety.quote: Both malignancies were assessed as not attributed to ROCTAVIAN based on vector insertion site analysis and whole genome sequencing. No cases of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) were reported.
safety.reason: Dogs' no-inhibitor, no-tumour calls hold so far

added_models.model: Hemophilia A mice, hepatic AAV-FVIII overexpression (ER-stress / unfolded-protein-response model)

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 27738645, epub 2016-09-28); AAV8 vectors from CHOP, not a member product.
safety.judgement: A distinct track from the sponsors' F8-KO mouse + macaque package: this system was built to ask whether FVIII load itself harms hepatocytes.
safety.note: CHOP hemophilia A mice: transient BiP/CHOP activation only with single-chain FVIII above 200% of normal, no change in liver function.
safety.short: Mice: ER stress only at >200% FVIII
safety.quote: These studies suggest that supraphysiological single chain FVIII expression may increase the likelihood of a cellular stress response but does not alter liver function.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 32775496, epub 2020-07-09). Whether this study is in the BLA pharmacology section could not be checked: the SBRA nonclinical text is partly redacted.
safety.judgement: Same model system, now run with the clinical construct; prediction for patients: no ER stress at the clinical promoter/dose.
safety.note: BioMarin's own AAV5-hFVIII-SQ mice: ER-stress markers rose only with a stronger promoter at the top dose, not with valoctocogene's HLP promoter.
safety.short: Product's promoter: no ER stress in mice
safety.quote: For 100ATGB, liver hFVIII-SQ protein accumulated dose dependently, with increased expression of ER stress markers at the highest dose, suggesting hepatocytes reached or exceeded their capacity to fold/secrete hFVIII-SQ.

safety.magnitude_basis: hepatocyte ER-stress markers (GRP78/BiP) in FVIII-expressing cells: none in mice with the clinical promoter, none in 5 patient biopsies
safety.confidence_note: Full text via PMC9018415; Fong 2022 cites Lange 2016 and its own mice but does not set them beside the biopsies, so paired by me. The mouse harm was conditional on >200% FVIII or a stronger promoter, conditions patients never reached (peak ~60-100%, lower at biopsy), so only the no-stress half of the prediction is tested; n=5, single late time point.
safety.judgement: Scored same, not contra/opposite: the model never predicted ER stress at the levels patients reached. A contra would need patients at supraphysiologic FVIII with stress, or stress at therapeutic levels.
safety.note: Liver biopsies 2.6-4.1 years after valoctocogene: FVIII-SQ-expressing hepatocytes showed no GRP78 rise and no ER stress, as the mice predicted at therapeutic levels.
safety.quote: Histopathology revealed no dysplasia, architectural distortion, fibrosis or chronic inflammation, and no endoplasmic reticulum stress was detected in hepatocytes expressing hFVIII-SQ protein.
safety.reason: No ER stress at therapeutic FVIII, as predicted

added_models.model: Hemophilia A mice, AAV8-hFVIII under rapamycin: post-clinic model of FVIII expression loss (Butterfield 2022)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 35821634, epub 2022-07-12); University of Florida / Indiana University, AAV8-hFVIII, not a member product.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry for a retrodiction track (decision 10); the flag sits on the scored entry, not this one. The checker's lead called this an NHP model; the primary paper is a mouse.
engagement.note: Mouse model built after valoctocogene and SPK-8011 patients lost FVIII expression; declines without antibodies while vector DNA and mRNA persist.
engagement.quote: However, declining therapeutic coagulation factor VIII (FVIII) expression has plagued clinical trials.

engagement.magnitude_basis: FVIII protein decline with persistent vector genomes and mRNA: mice over months vs valoctocogene patients over years (Fong 2022 biopsies show persistent FVIII-SQ RNA)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The mouse needed rapamycin co-treatment and initial FVIII >100% to decline, conditions not matched in patients; the human mechanism (translational shutdown, IL-15) is unproven. Registry date is the NCT02576795 results posting.
engagement.judgement: Status retro, never same (decision 10): the clinic already knew FVIII fell. Placed in engagement because the retrodicted quantity is the transgene-protein readout over time; no prospective prediction from this model has been tested in patients.
engagement.note: The model reproduces the clinical pattern: FVIII protein falls over time without inhibitors despite persistent transgene and mRNA, with ER stress in some animals.
engagement.quote: To assess the mechanistic underpinnings of this loss of FVIII expression, we developed a hemophilia A mouse model that shares key features observed in clinical trials.
engagement.reason: Retrodiction of the clinical FVIII decline

added_models.model: Cynomolgus macaques with pre-existing anti-AAV5 antibodies given valoctocogene roxaparvovec (BMN 270)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 31193016, epub 2019-04-11); BioMarin's own study with the clinical product at 6e13 vg/kg.
engagement.judgement: A patient-level track: the model picks who responds (antibody-negative) rather than whether the class works. Whether this study is in the BLA could not be read; the SBRA nonclinical text is partly redacted.
engagement.note: Monkeys with pre-existing AAV5 antibodies had 74.8% lower FVIII-SQ Cmax and fewer liver vector genomes; non-antibody inhibitors did not matter.
engagement.quote: These results demonstrate that animals without AAV5 antibodies are likely responders to AAV5 gene therapy, regardless of other inhibiting plasma factors.

engagement.magnitude_basis: FVIII expression in AAV5-antibody-positive recipients of 6e13 vg/kg: monkeys 74.8% lower Cmax than non-immune controls; patients 1/3 ≥5 IU/dL at week 26 (study 270-203) vs 132/134 ≥5 IU/dL in antibody-negative GENEr8-1
engagement.confidence_note: Registry record only (results posted 2025-08-22; trial terminated for rollover, 3 enrolled, 2 did not complete). No per-patient antibody titres, so the model's titre threshold is untested; all 3 reported an ABR reduction. Paired by me. The US label restricts to antibody-negative patients by the AAV5 DetectCDx companion diagnostic, but the regulator relied on trial exclusion, not on this model in lieu of a trial.
engagement.judgement: Direction agrees (antibody-positive recipients under-express) but n=3 and the registry gives counts, not levels; low confidence rather than untested because a comparison can be made.
engagement.note: Three AAV5-antibody-positive men at 6e13 vg/kg: 1 of 3 reached FVIII ≥5 IU/dL at week 26, with FVIII use continuing, the blunted response monkeys showed.
engagement.quote: Number of Participant With FVIII Activity >= 5 IU/dL at Week 26. Using Chromogenic Substrate Assay (CSA).

added_models.model: FVIII-knockout mice + cynomolgus macaques given AAVhu37.E03.TTR.hFVIIIco-SQ (BAY 2599023 / DTX201, peboctocogene camaparvovec)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 28056565, epub 2017-01-05). No FDA/EMA review exists for this unapproved product.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry for the tile member with no track in the draft; the member's own model, not the sponsors' pooled mouse + macaque track.
engagement.note: Dimension/Penn screened 42 promoter-enhancer cassettes and five capsids in FVIII-KO mice; AAVhu37 was among the more immunogenic capsids in mice.
engagement.quote: The capsids subdivided into two groups: those that generated anti-hFVIII antibodies in ≤20% of mice (AAV8 and AAV9), and those that generated anti-hFVIII antibodies in >20% of mice (AAVrh10, AAVhu37, and AAVrh64R1).

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 29890905). Phase 1/2 NCT03588299 (Bayer, n=11, completed 2026-09-15) has no posted results; FVIII activity in patients is reported only in ASH/ISTH abstracts ('stable and sustained expression of FVIII over 2 years') and was 'NR' in the 2024 Blood Advances meta-analysis, so no tier 1-5 patient source exists.
engagement.judgement: Untested, not blank: the model existed and was the product's basis, but the only patient data are conference abstracts, outside the source tiers.
engagement.note: Macaques at 1.2e13 GC/kg of the clinical candidate expressed 20% hFVIII at two weeks, then mostly made anti-hFVIII antibodies; patients: conference abstracts only.
engagement.quote: Two weeks after administration of E03.TTR packaged within the AAVhu37 capsid, average hFVIII expression was 20.2 ± 5.0% of normal, with one animal exhibiting peak expression of 37.1% of normal hFVIII levels.
engagement.reason: No admissible patient result to compare

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 34652966, epub 2021-12-08). Patient dose range from the 2024 Blood Advances meta-analysis table (NCT03588299: 5e12, 1e13, 2e13, 4e13).
dose.judgement: Dose cell opens at the MED study rather than 2017 because the earlier papers set no exposure target.
dose.note: Mouse minimally effective dose 3e11 GC/kg and MTD ≥1e13 GC/kg for the clinical candidate; patients received 5e12-4e13 GC/kg, with no posted results to compare.
dose.quote: Studies in mice and macaques identified AAVhu37.E03.TTR.hFVIIIco-SQ.PA75 as a clinical candidate gene therapy vector to treat hemophilia A.
dose.reason: No posted patient PK or FVIII levels

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 34652966). The trial's primary outcome is adverse events, but no results are posted and no label or review exists.
safety.judgement: Untested; a mouse cannot show capsid T-cell hepatitis, so its silence there would not be a miss even once patient data appear.
safety.note: Mouse toxicology of the clinical candidate: no transaminase rise or vector-related histology up to 1e13 GC/kg; patient safety (primary endpoint of NCT03588299) not posted.
safety.quote: We observed no vector-related gross or histological findings.

added_models.model: C57BL/6 mice given human serum then AAV6-hF9 (passive-transfer neutralization model) setting the anti-AAV6 antibody enrollment cutoff for giroctocogene fitelparvovec (SB-525)

engagement.confidence_note: Full text (PMC9935387, epub 2022-07-01), Sangamo authors; the mice received an AAV6-hF9 vector, not the product, so product_in_model false. Date of the mouse runs is not given; dated to publication.
engagement.judgement: Patient-level track: the model picks who can respond by pre-existing AAV6 antibody titre. Opening untested entry at first published use.
engagement.note: Mice given human sera with AAV6 transduction-inhibition NR >0.33 still made therapeutic hFIX; only NR <0.1 fully blocked expression, supporting a 0.34 enrollment cutoff.
engagement.short: Mice: NR >0.33 serum still allows expression
engagement.quote: Though the results are highly variable, animals exposed to human serum with NR > 0.33 on average still produced levels of hFIX (>150 ng/mL) that are considered therapeutic

engagement.magnitude_basis: Mice: serum NR >0.33 permits therapeutic transgene expression; Alta (NCT03061201) patients enrolled at NR 0.38-1.11 all showed dose-dependent FVIII activity, normal range in cohort 4 (3e13 vg/kg)
engagement.confidence_note: Sponsor states the comparison in the same paper. Only the antibody-low half of the prediction was tested: no patient below the 0.34 cutoff was dosed, so the threshold itself is untested.
engagement.judgement: Same: every patient the model-set cutoff admitted expressed FVIII, as the mice predicted; the prediction was set before Alta enrolled, so not a retrodiction.
engagement.note: All 11 Alta participants, enrolled at NR 0.38-1.11 under the mouse-supported cutoff, expressed FVIII dose-dependently with giroctocogene.
engagement.quote: The cutoff of 0.34 thus led to enrollment of hemophilia A subjects that responded to AAV6 gene therapy treatment.
engagement.reason: Antibody-low patients expressed, as mice predicted

added_models.model: Hemophilia A mice given AAV-FVIII-SQ: post-clinic model of the one-stage vs chromogenic assay discrepancy and FVIII-SQ activation (Sternberg 2026, SPK-8011 comparison)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 42371804, epub 2026-06-29); CHOP/Roche authors; vector identity in mice not stated in the abstract, so product_in_model false.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry for a retrodiction track (decision 10); the flag sits on the scored entry.
engagement.note: Mouse model built after AAV trials showed one-stage FVIII-SQ activity 1.5-2x chromogenic values; tests cofactor function and thrombin activation of AAV-derived FVIII-SQ.
engagement.short: Post-clinic mouse of FVIII-SQ assay gap
engagement.quote: In vivo evaluation of AAV-FVIII-SQ in mice demonstrated that OSA activity better correlated with hemostatic function and corresponded to rFVIII-SQ function.

engagement.magnitude_basis: Enhanced thrombin-mediated activation of AAV-FVIII-SQ, seen by one-stage but not chromogenic assay, in mice and in SPK-8011 (dirloctocogene) participants; 23 participants, 99 patient-years
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The patient assay discrepancy was known from the trials before the mouse work, hence a retrodiction; the ABR association in patients was only a trend.
engagement.judgement: Status retro, never same: the clinic already knew one-stage exceeded chromogenic activity; the mouse reproduces the patient biochemistry.
engagement.note: Mice and SPK-8011 participants both showed normal cofactor function and enhanced thrombin activation of AAV-derived FVIII-SQ.
engagement.quote: Both species demonstrated enhanced thrombin-mediated activation of AAV-FVIII-SQ, detectable by OSA but not CSA.
engagement.reason: Retrodiction of the patient assay discrepancy

considered_not_added: Kistner 2024 (doi:10.1038/s41434-023-00423-z) cynomolgus macaques given AAVrh10-hFVIII under prophylactic immunosuppression (Ultragenyx/Penn): sibling capsid, not a member product, and it asks a regimen question (prednisolone +/- rapamycin), not whether the class works; the nearest patient test is GENEr8-3 prophylactic corticosteroids (NCT04323098, results 2024-04-04) but no source states the comparison

Elkouby 2022 (doi:10.1016/j.omtm.2021.11.005) SPK-8011 (dirloctocogene) mice + non-human primates with Spark100/Spark200 capsids: the same system as the draft's hema-f8ko-mouse-nhp track, so not a new model

Humanized-liver (FRG / human-hepatocyte chimeric) mice: no hemophilia A gene-therapy hits on PubMed; the LK03 capsid selection in humanized mice (Lisowski 2014) was not tied to any F8 patient comparison within budget
Simoctocog alfa (Nuwiq) preclinical hemophilia A mouse / immunogenicity model: no PubMed hits for simoctocog with mice or preclinical; no model comparison found

BAY 2599023 patient FVIII data: exist only as ASH/ISTH conference abstracts ('stable and sustained expression of FVIII over 2 years'), NR in the 2024 meta-analysis, no registry results; the AAVhu37 track is therefore added as untested rather than scored
Gil-Farina 2016 NHP and patient AAV integration (cited by Fong 2022): hemophilia B AAV2-FIX patients, cross-class evidence set aside (decision 13)
Efanesoctocog alfa population-PK / in-silico dose models: not searched within budget (clinical PK models, not a preclinical system)

The ER-stress and FVIII-decline mice could be argued onto the draft's pooled hema-f8ko-mouse-nhp track; kept as their own tracks because that track's safety strip is contra (ALT) and cannot take a later same, and because each system was built to ask a different question (decision 10 for the retrodiction)

SPK-8016: no published preclinical model for the product; the inhibitor-dog tolerance work (Finn 2010) was never compared with SPK-8016 patients because the inhibitor study it was to support never ran; NCT03734588 results are non-inhibitor dose-finding with no model named
Giroctocogene (SB-525) mouse/NHP potency studies: conference abstracts only, no peer-reviewed model-to-patient comparison found

Kistner 2024 macaque steroid/rapamycin regimens (AAVrh10): GENEr8-3 (NCT04323098) was designed and enrolled before Kistner and is single-arm (FVIII change at week 52, no steroid-free comparator), so the model's 'not sustained upon taper' prediction has no clean patient test; no source states the comparison
